newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
CORRUPTION TO BE BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY PLANK

Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president L.K. Advani started his "Rath Yatra" (march) across 20 states from Bombay by lambasting the Congress, the Left and the Janata Dal for engaging in a power struggle. Advani called for banishing the evils of hunger, fear and corruption from the country. The seven-week yatra, virtually kick-starting the BJP's campaign for likely mid-term polls, would skip the sensitive northeastern states and Kashmir.
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS CHIEF DENIES BEING IN RACE FOR PRESIDENT'S POST

Congress president Sitaram Kesri said he was not in the reckoning for the presidency of India. He denied he was encouraging members of parliament to canvass support for his candidature. He also refuted charges that he was soft on corruption or wanted to rig the ongoing party polls. Kesri said Congress would work out its strategy for the selection of the next president in consultation with other secular parties.
The Times Of India
CONGRESS PARTY POLLS RUN INTO ROUGH WEATHER

The Congress party's organisational elections were in serious problems with various state units driven with factional differences. Even as the party chief's intervention was being sought, demands were being made for Sonia Gandhi to play an active role in the organisation and to take over the leadership.
The Economic Times
FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT ON TOP

For the first time in the recent past foreign direct investment (FDI) at $2.59 billion had overtaken net portfolio investment by foreign institutional investors (FIIs). It now has the largest share -- 40.22 percent -- of the total foreign investment in 1996/97. This is significant since FDI was viewed as a more stable and qualitatively better form of foreign investment compared to FII portfolio investment. If this trend continues, the $10-billion annual FDI inflow target might be achieved sooner than envisaged.
TELCO PLANS $200 MLN YANKEE BOND ISSUE

Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO), India's largest private sector automobile company, will tap the Yankee bond market in the next couple of months. The TELCO board will meet on May 26 to consider the bond issue. The issue is likely to be about $200 million. Merrill Lynch, CS First Boston and J.P. Morgan were said to be among the prominent investment bankers vying for the mandate. While Telco had to date made two GDR issues of $200 million and $115 million, the proposed issue would be its first international bond offering.
50,000 RUPEE CAP ON STOCKINVEST TO CURB MISUSE

Misuse of the stock invest instrument has compelled the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to put a blanket ceiling of 50,000 rupees per instrument. Sources in the RBI said it has already written to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) that it would tell the banks of its inability to issue instruments over this limit.
FOREIGN, NON RESIDENT EQUITY ON A PAR IN BROADCASTING

Foreign equity in broadcasting companies might not be treated as distinct from investments made by non-resident Indians (NRIs). The Information and Broadcasting Ministry recommended guidelines on the definition of foreign equity should be drawn up on the basis of regulations in the telecomminication sector. Going by this, NRI equity would be treated as the same as holdings of foreign companies. As a result, the 49 percent cap on foreign equity stipulated in the Broadcast Bill would be the limit of total holdings of NRI/overseas corporate bodies and foreign companies, ministry officials said.
Financial Express
MINISTRY SAYS IMPORTED AUSTRALIAN WHEAT INFECTED

The Agriculture Ministry has warned the Food Corporation of India (FCI) that imported Australian wheat might be contaminated and the situation could be alarming. The ministry's plant quarantine division has told the FCI there was evidence of exotic weed seeds in the wheat samples taken from Indian ports. If the weeds got established in Indian soil, it would be detrimental to crops and the agricultural economy. The letter emphasised that it was imperative that no weed seed should be allowed entry into the country. Roughly 1.2 million tonnes of Australian wheat has already reached Indian shores.
INDIA TO BUY 3000 MW POWER FROM PAKISTAN

India has decided to purchase 3000 megawatts of surplus power from Pakistan generated from the hydroelectric resources of the Indus river basin. Power Minister S. Venugopalachari said discussions would be initiated at the secretary level soon. The government proposed to tap power from Pakistan through a transmission line from Punjab to Lahore. The plan was expected to become operational by 1998/99.
Business Standard
PEUGEOT LOOKING FOR NEW INDIAN PARTNER

French automobile major Peugeot will search for a new Indian partner. Peugeot's decision followed its overtures to its present partners to buy out their stake in the joint venture, PAD Peugeot. Both sides hold a 31.7 percent equity stake each in PAD Peugeot, which had accumulated losses of 920 million rupees since it began commercial operations. The French Ministry of Industrial Strategy said the only way out for the troubled venture was for Peugeot to buy up the partner's stake and then off load it to another Indian partner, as and when one would be identified.
MOBIL GETS CLEARANCE FOR 10 PCT HOLDING COMPANY

The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) has approved U.S.-based oil giant Mobil Corporation's proposal to set up a 100 percent holding company in India. It would be one of the first oil majors to set up its own Indian subsidiary for pursuing investment activities. Mobil plans to bring in $5 million as initial equity capital to establish Mobil Asia Pacific Private Limited. The company would utilise its subsidiary to transfer its proprietary technology to various projects in the country and explore investment opportunities in the high-cost power, liquefied natural gas, petrochemicals and oil-related sectors in the country.
INTERNATIONAL PRICES FOR PRIVATE CRUDE PRODUCERS

Private sector oil companies which produce crude oil from oil fields discovered by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India Limited (OIL) will soon receive international prices for the oil they produce. The government has started informing the companies about its decision. The field's owner will be entitled to receive 40 percent of the proceeds from sale of the crude. ONGC will now receive international prices for the crude oil it produces from the fields for which it had production sharing contracts with private operators. OIL will also be paid at international rates for its share of production.
FOREIGN BIDDING IN DIAMOND MINING RECOMMENDED

An expert group set up by the Madhya Pradesh government has endorsed the entry of multinationals into diamond exploration and mining. It has recommended that foreign mining companies should collaborate with the State Mining Corporation to take up mining in the state. Companies that want to set up 100 percent subsidiaries might be allowed to do so, provided they obtain foreign investment promotion board approval to raise their stake in the joint venture above 50 per cent. If the report were to be implemented, Madhya Pradesh would be the first Indian state to open up diamond mining to the private sector.
The Observer
INFLATION DECLINES BELOW SIX PERCENT

The annual rate of inflation fell by 0.37 percentage point to below the six percent mark as it touched 5.98 percent for the week ending May 3. This was the eighth week in succession that inflation maintained a downward trend. The decline was attributed to a fall in prices of wheat, vegetables, eggs and fruits, among other goods.
